A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 21-page versions of the same research work. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison cover the main text, equations, figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–F without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original BabiLong and RULER experiments and ablations in Section 5, plus MoE, RAMba, and inference-latency results in Appendices A, D, and E.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original benchmark evaluations, architectural ablations, retrieval diagnostics, and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The SWA+HSA procedure, chunk encoder and CLS token, bypassing residual path, and Appendix D RAMba-MLP adaptation are identical.

E1.justification: Both retain the same Pile-based training, 20 BabiLong tasks, three RULER tasks, and seven general-capability benchmarks in Appendix A. No datasets, tasks, or test scenarios change.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Figure 3 and Tables 2, 4, 6, and 7, including the same Transformer-MoE and RAMba comparisons in the appendices.

E3.justification: Model sizes, training budgets, context lengths, metrics, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Appendix E.2 retains the latency protocol of generating 100 tokens with batch size 16, excluding prefilling.

E4.justification: Both contain identical encoder/CLS/bypass ablations, retrieval and integration diagnostics in Figure 4, sparsity experiments in Table 3, and RAMba analyses in Appendix D.

E5.justification: Both retain the same point-estimate and task-average reporting, without repeated-run or seed statistics, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, plotted results, and reported findings are identical. For example, Table 2 retains 87.92% at 4K and 79.77% at 32M for the two-layer encoder model with CLS and bypass.

T1.justification: The Random Context Access definition, attention and landmark mathematics, residual equations, and Appendix E.1 complexity derivations are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same architectural design principles, contributions, and claim of training-free extrapolation from 4K to 32M tokens.

C2.justification: The explanations of retrieval prominence, information integration, sparsity tradeoffs, scalability, and efficiency are identical. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added or removed.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains identical hyperparameters, tokenizer information, data construction, and training recipes. The repository link and code/data-access statements also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Appendix B, and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning relative to earlier sparse-attention, retrieval, and recurrent architectures.

P1.justification: The running header changes from 'Accepted to ICLR 2026. Final version to appear.' to 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026'. The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 5 February 2026 to v3 dated 30 April 2026. All other text and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–5 and Tables 1–7 retain identical visuals, captions, formatting, and placement. Rendered page bodies match throughout, including the appendices; the header and version-stamp wording updates do not reorganize the layout.

improvement.justification: v3 updates publication and version labels only. The scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information, and visual presentation remain unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
